OSPS-AC-01.01.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and accepts only secure methods, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

OSPS-AC-02.01.justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission. Every higher grant is assigned by hand. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/REPOSITORY.md

OSPS-AC-03.01.justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor holds it in pull_request mode, which never allows a direct push. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-03.02.justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-04.01.justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-AC-04.02.justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds only the write scopes it uses. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does

OSPS-BR-01.01.justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

OSPS-BR-01.03.justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. The issue_comment job, which holds a secret on any pull request, checks out the default branch. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml

OSPS-BR-01.04.justification: The only workflow_dispatch input is mutation.yml's profile, a choice from a fixed list. A release tag's name is checked against the package version before anything is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml

OSPS-BR-02.01.justification: Each release has a unique calendar version (YYYY.M.D), set by a signed v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that disagrees with the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/releases

OSPS-BR-02.02.justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name: the sdist, the wheel, the CycloneDX SBOM and the attestation bundle. The attestation binds each asset to its digest. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-03.01.justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://btclib-ecc.readthedocs.io/.

OSPS-BR-03.02.justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-ecc/

OSPS-BR-04.01.justification: The GitHub release body is RELEASE_NOTES.md's entry: what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included. CHANGELOG.md lists every change. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

OSPS-BR-05.01.justification: Pipelines install dependencies with uv: from the committed uv.lock with --locked, except the jobs that test a fresh resolution and the build backend, which uv build takes within pyproject.toml's uv_build range. The post-release install check uses pip. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock

OSPS-BR-06.01.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. The GitHub release carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle over each asset's SHA-256. The tag is signed. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-07.01.justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.secrets.baseline

OSPS-BR-07.02.justification: A secret is an environment secret only the owners reach, and any other store's entry is recorded in the spending repository's REPOSITORY.md. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected, and the list is reviewed yearly. btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded entry. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2913-L2940

OSPS-DO-01.01.justification: The user documentation is README.md's First use section, which tests/readme_test.py runs, and the API reference at https://btclib-ecc.readthedocs.io/.

OSPS-DO-02.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report form asks for what a report needs. SECURITY.md sends a vulnerability to a private channel instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml

OSPS-DO-03.01.justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release assets, and RELEASING.md the check that rebuilds the sdist from its tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-03.02.justification: The verify command pins the signer: --repo names this repository, --signer-workflow the organization's reusable-build.yml (reusable-attest.yml for earlier releases) and --source-ref the release tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-04.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, a fix ships as a new release, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-05.01.justification: SECURITY.md: only the latest release is supported, so a release stops receiving security updates when the next one is published. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-06.01.justification: pyproject.toml gives the reason for each runtime dependency. uv obtains them from PyPI and pins them in uv.lock, and Dependabot tracks them weekly with a seven-day cooldown. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci

OSPS-DO-07.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-01.01.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's Roles names who holds access to sensitive resources: the maintainer, the only bypass actor, and the three owners, each an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-01.02.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* describes the maintainer, owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-02.01.justification: Proposed changes and usage obstacles are discussed publicly in the repository's GitHub issues (with a question form) and pull requests; cross-repository questions go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/issues

OSPS-GV-03.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-03.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% line and branch coverage, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-04.01.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/GOVERNANCE.md#L44-L46 : a grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there.

OSPS-LE-01.01.justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, so a pull request cannot merge unless every commit carries its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Web commits are signed off automatically. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

OSPS-LE-02.01.justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-02.02.justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-ecc/

OSPS-LE-03.01.justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-03.02.justification: The LICENSE file ships inside every release asset: the sdist root and the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-QA-01.01.justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc

OSPS-QA-01.02.justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature; linear history and no force-pushes on main keep that record from being rewritten. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/commits/main

OSPS-QA-02.01.justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies ([project] dependencies, optional extras and dependency groups), and the committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-02.02.justification: Every release attaches a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM generated from the built wheel, listing its dependencies and covered by the release attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/releases/latest

OSPS-QA-03.01.justification: main requires the five CI status checks, up to date with main (strict). enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without them is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-QA-04.01.justification: The organization standard's section 2 (*Which repositories, and how far*) lists every repository of btclib-org and its tier, and the organization profile lists the published packages. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far

OSPS-QA-04.02.justification: Each release is built from this single repository; the sibling packages it depends on are released separately from their own repositories, which are held to the same standard. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc

OSPS-QA-05.01.justification: No generated executable is committed. The only binary files are fuzz seed inputs and the Sphinx inventory python.inv, and the lint gate's check-added-large-files keeps build output out.

OSPS-QA-05.02.justification: No executable, library or compiled file is committed. The only binary files are fuzz seed inputs under fuzz/corpus and docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, none of them code.

OSPS-QA-06.01.justification: test.yml's aggregate check ('test: every job passed') runs the test suite on every pull request and is a required status check on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

OSPS-QA-06.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite and which workflows run it on every pull request, on main and on a schedule, and which of them gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-QA-06.03.justification: The policy is 100% line and branch coverage (CONTRIBUTING.md, standard section 8). pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, so untested new code fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-07.01.justification: main's ruleset requires one approving review, but the maintainer's pull_request-mode bypass remains, and recent pull requests landed without a non-author approval. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#review

OSPS-SA-01.01.justification: CLAUDE.md's Architecture gives the components and their layering. ASSURANCE_CASE.md's Threat model and Trust boundaries name the actors and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#architecture

OSPS-SA-02.01.justification: The API reference at https://btclib-ecc.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module, and tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from it. CONTRIBUTING.md's The public surface states what is public.

OSPS-SA-03.01.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: what is claimed, the threat model, the trust boundaries and how each common implementation weakness is countered; SECURITY.md's limitations section records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-SA-03.02.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names the assets, adversaries and what is not defended, and *Trust boundaries* maps the attack surface where untrusted input enters, each argument naming the file, test or workflow behind it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-VM-01.01.justification: SECURITY.md gives the private reporting channels and states the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L19

OSPS-VM-02.01.justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org, which reaches the three organization owners. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-VM-03.01.justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/security/advisories/new

OSPS-VM-04.01.justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository, each naming the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/security/advisories

OSPS-VM-04.02.justification: Each release's CycloneDX SBOM lists in its vulnerabilities array every vulnerability judged not to affect it, with the reason, from the tree's .github/vex.toml. None is judged so today, so the tree has no such file. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L3120-L3135

OSPS-VM-05.01.justification: Every pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action, which fails on an added or changed dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909

OSPS-VM-05.02.justification: release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares before any publish job. An advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id the release's own signed VEX states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L3149-L3160

OSPS-VM-05.03.justification: The Dependency review job runs on every pull request and is a required check on main (lint / Dependency review), so a pull request that violates the policy cannot merge. Policy: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909

OSPS-VM-06.01.justification: The standard's section 5 sets the threshold at zero: ruff runs select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same. CodeQL alerts have no stated threshold. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff

OSPS-VM-06.02.justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml

access_continuity.justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an administrator of this repository and a reviewer of its publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity

accessibility_best_practices.justification: btclib-ecc is a library with no user interface: no CLI, no GUI and no web front end, so accessibility best practices have no surface to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/README.md

assurance_case.justification: The assurance case is https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md: threat model, trust boundaries, the argument that secure design principles are applied, and how common implementation weaknesses are countered.

automated_integration_testing.justification: test.yml runs the test suite, with and without the libsecp256k1 bindings, on every push to main and every pull request, and its aggregate job `test: every job passed` is a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

build_non_recursive.justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_preserve_debug.justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_repeatable.justification: Pure-Python source is used directly (uv_build, no compilation step), so there is nothing whose bit-for-bit regeneration to test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_reproducible.justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit and normalized by normalize_sdist.py, and sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release from its signed tag and runs `gh attestation verify` over the rebuilt file against the release's build-provenance attestation; RELEASING.md tells a user how to do the same. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml

build_standard_variables.justification: This tree builds no native binaries -- it is pure Python on the uv_build backend -- so there is no compiler or linker invocation for CC/CFLAGS/LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

bus_factor.justification: Almost every commit is the maintainer's, and one other person has landed one pull request. Continuity rests on the three organization owners, each an administrator of this repository. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

code_of_conduct.justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

code_review_standards.justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/REVIEWING.md

coding_standards.justification: pyproject.toml selects every ruff rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and runs mypy in strict mode. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

coding_standards_enforced.justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run as pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs the same .pre-commit-config.yaml in CI as a required check, so the style is enforced automatically rather than by review alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

contribution_requirements.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the coding-standard, input-validation, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

contributors_unassociated.justification: The project has one significant contributor; one other person has contributed once.

copyright_per_file.justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/src/btclib_ecc/__init__.py

crypto_algorithm_agility.justification: btclib-ecc implements every curve SEC 2, NIST and Brainpool define, not only secp256k1, and its signature and nonce functions take the curve and the hash function as parameters. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/README.md

crypto_call.justification: primary purpose is to implement cryptography

crypto_certificate_verification.justification: btclib-ecc performs no network communications -- nothing under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib -- and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/tree/main/src/btclib_ecc

crypto_credential_agility.justification: btclib-ecc is a library with no configuration file or credential store: a private key is a caller-supplied function parameter, never read from or written to a file this project owns. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

crypto_keylength.justification: Every default is secp256k1, about 128 bits of security, above NIST's 112-bit floor for 2030. Smaller curves are in the catalogue only by name, the SEC 2 v1 ones kept apart as insecure. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/README.md

crypto_pfs.justification: implements no network key-agreement protocol: dh and ecies are primitives, and whether a session built on them is forward-secret is the calling protocol's choice

crypto_published.justification: The Python arithmetic implements published algorithms (SEC 1, RFC 6979, BIP340, BIP327, draft BIP445, BIP374, BIP324) and is validated against the specifications' own vectors. On secp256k1, with the optional bindings installed, a call delegates to Bitcoin Core's libsecp256k1 wherever its guard admits it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/README.md

crypto_random.justification: Private keys, MuSig2, FROST and DLEQ nonces, BIP340 auxiliary randomness, ECIES ephemeral keys and blinding factors come from Python's secrets module. ECDSA nonces are deterministic (RFC 6979), and nothing under src/ uses the random module. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/tree/main/src/btclib_ecc

crypto_tls12.justification: btclib-ecc performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/tree/main/src/btclib_ecc

crypto_used_network.justification: btclib-ecc does not use the network: nothing under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/tree/main/src/btclib_ecc

crypto_verification_private.justification: btclib-ecc performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/tree/main/src/btclib_ecc

crypto_weaknesses.justification: Every default is secp256k1 with SHA-256, and no SHA-1 or MD5 appears under src/. The SEC 2 v1 curves that SEC 2 v2 withdrew are kept apart as insecure. ECIES checks its MAC with hmac.compare_digest before calling the caller's cipher. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

dco.justification: Every commit carries its author's Signed-off-by: trailer: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit lacking it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

dependency_monitoring.justification: Dependabot version updates cover uv, github-actions and docker, and Dependabot security updates are on. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml

discussion.justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.

documentation_achievements.justification: README.md shows the OpenSSF Scorecard, Best Practices and Baseline badges together. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/README.md

documentation_architecture.justification: CLAUDE.md's Architecture gives the layers bottom-up (number_theory and hashes, curves/, ecc/), the rule that ecc imports curves and never the reverse, and the one module that imports the libsecp256k1 bindings. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#architecture

documentation_basics.justification: Some documentation basics file contents found.

documentation_current.justification: The docs build is gated in CI as a required check (docs.yml, `-n -W`), and tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module has no API page, so the reference generated from the docstrings cannot drift from the code. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml

documentation_interface.justification: Every public module and function carries a docstring, gated by ruff's pydocstyle rules and pydoclint, and docs/source's automodule pages render them into the API reference; tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/tree/main/docs/source

documentation_quick_start.justification: The README's "First use" section (https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc#first-use) shows an ECDSA and a BIP340 sign-and-verify; tests/readme_test.py runs it in the test suite.

documentation_roadmap.justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, covers the period until 2027-09-30, is reviewed every September, and states what is intended and what is deliberately not; this tree's README.md links it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md

documentation_security.justification: SECURITY.md's Limitations, not vulnerabilities states what a user can and cannot expect: constant-time behaviour, key zeroization, and which operations delegate to libsecp256k1. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions.justification: pytest runs the test suite and the fuzz targets without -O, so assert statements stay enabled during dynamic analysis.

dynamic_analysis_unsafe.justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

external_dependencies.justification: Every dependency is declared in machine-readable form in pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies], optional-dependencies and dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

floss_license.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

floss_license_osi.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

governance.justification: GOVERNANCE.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, documents the decision model, the maintainer's bypass and every role a contributor, reviewer or owner holds; this tree's README.md links it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

hardened_site.justification: https://btclib.org/btclib-ecc/ is served over HTTPS with Content-Security-Policy (frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security.

hardening.justification: ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules, so a hardening defect such as unsafe deserialization or shell injection fails the lint gate. CodeQL also runs on every pull request and every push to main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

implement_secure_design.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* section argues how each principle is applied, and SECURITY.md records the design decisions where a secret meets the curve. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

input_validation.justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid with a BTClibEccTypeError or BTClibEccValueError; the unchecked work lives in a private twin the public function calls once it has validated, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_common.justification: The package is on PyPI, so `pip install btclib-ecc` (or `pip uninstall`) is the commonly-used convention for installing and removing it; README.md gives the exact command, with the "secp256k1" extra. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/README.md

installation_development_quick.justification: `uv sync` installs the whole development environment in one command; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* section gives it beside `uv run pytest` and the lint gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_standard_variables.justification: Installation is `pip install`, which follows pip's and the interpreter's own install-location conventions; there is no project-specific installer that could diverge from that convention. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

interfaces_current.justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated constructs, and pytest turns every warning into an error. deps-latest and deps-oldest run the suite weekly at the newest and the floor versions. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

internationalization.justification: btclib-ecc generates no end-user-facing text and sorts no human-readable strings for a locale; its output (integers, octets, points, signatures) is technical data, not text meant for localization. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/README.md

know_common_errors.justification: The primary developer wrote ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Common implementation weaknesses*, which names each error class for this code and the test or check that counters it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

know_secure_design.justification: The primary developer wrote ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles*, which argues how each is applied here. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

license_location.justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/LICENSE>.

license_per_file.justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/src/btclib_ecc/__init__.py

maintenance_or_update.justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported (SECURITY.md). RELEASING.md runs griffe check against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists what a user must act on to upgrade. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

regression_tests_added50.justification: Every merged pull request that changes src/ also changes tests/, bar one that only edits docstrings (#155). The 100% line and branch coverage gate also fails a fix whose new code no test runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged

release_notes.justification: Non-trivial release notes file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md>.

release_notes_vulns.justification: The release notes name each advisory the release fixes: v2026.10.8 names GHSA-2wgq-4cfh-5gqh. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/releases/tag/v2026.10.8

repo_distributed.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.

repo_interim.justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc

repo_public.justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.

repo_track.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.

report_process.justification: Non-trivial SECURITY[.md] file found file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md>. [osps_do_02_01]

report_tracker.justification: Each repository uses its own GitHub Issues tracker for individual issues, with issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and an organization-wide tracker in btclib-org/.github for cross-repository findings. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/issues

require_2FA.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member. https://github.com/btclib-org

roles_responsibilities.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's Roles names the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

secure_2FA.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication and allows only secure methods: TOTP apps, security keys or passkeys, and GitHub Mobile, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

security_review.justification: pmazzocchi, an owner other than the maintainer, reviewed the project on 2026-09-30: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/issues/84 . The review pins its scope to a commit, checks each claim of ASSURANCE_CASE.md, states what it did not cover and files each finding as an issue.

signed_releases.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing, and each GitHub release a Sigstore provenance bundle. SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/releases/latest

sites_password_security.justification: Project sites are GitHub, PyPI and Read the Docs; this repository runs no site of its own that stores user passwords -- authentication is GitHub's and PyPI's, not this project's. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

small_tasks.justification: Small tasks for new contributors carry the label "good first issue", which CONTRIBUTING.md sets aside for a first contribution. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities.justification: CodeQL's python analysis (codeql.yml) runs on a schedule, on every pull request and on every push to main, and ruff's `select = ["ALL"]` includes the bandit-derived S rules, both FLOSS static-analysis tools looking for common vulnerabilities. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

static_analysis_often.justification: on every push and pull request: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/actions/workflows/lint.yml, https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/actions/workflows/codeql.yml

test.justification: test.yml runs the suite, gated at 100% line and branch coverage, against vectors their authors publish: the BIPs', Wycheproof's, libsecp256k1-zkp's and RFC 6979's. tests/_data/README.md pins each vendored file to its upstream commit. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

test_branch_coverage80.justification: Branch coverage is measured (branch = true in [tool.coverage.run]) and the 100% gate (fail_under) includes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_policy_mandated.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% line and branch coverage, and fail_under = 100.0 fails the CI gate on any new code without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

test_statement_coverage80.justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0, gated on every pull request by test.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_statement_coverage90.justification: Coverage is gated at 100% (fail_under = 100.0 in [tool.coverage.report]) on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

tests_documented_added.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100% coverage gate, so new functionality is not accepted without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

two_person_review.justification: main's ruleset requires one approving review, but the maintainer's pull_request-mode bypass remains, and recent pull requests landed without a non-author approval. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#review

updateable_reused_components.justification: Reused components are either standard-library modules or PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock and bumped weekly by Dependabot, and the deps-latest sentinel runs the full suite against the upgraded set every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/.github/workflows/deps-latest.yml

version_semver.justification: Calendar versioning, YYYY.M.D, with the day as the micro level; each release is tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github#12-releasing

version_tags_signed.justification: Every release tag is signed, and RELEASING.md reads each signature back. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/tags

vulnerabilities_critical_fixed.justification: No publicly known vulnerability is left unfixed: each published advisory names the release that fixes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/security/advisories

vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days.justification: No publicly known vulnerability is left unpatched. Each was fixed in a release within two days of being reported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/security/advisories

vulnerability_report_credit.justification: pmazzocchi, who reported GHSA-r5pw-9wrg-m3mj and GHSA-m38m-987v-j55h, is credited as finder on both. GHSA-2wgq-4cfh-5gqh had no outside reporter: the maintainer filed it from an audit of the organization's trees. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/security/advisories

vulnerability_report_response.justification: Every vulnerability report so far was answered and fixed within two days of being filed. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/security/advisories

vulnerability_response_process.justification: SECURITY.md's Reporting a vulnerability gives the private channels (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who can see a report, and how a CVE is requested. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

warnings.justification: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_fixed.justification: warning are not tolerated: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_strict.justification: ruff runs with `select = ["ALL"]` (every rule family) and mypy runs with `strict = true`; both are zero-finding pre-commit hooks enforced again by the required lint workflow. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-ecc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
